title: Jalen Brunson: Second-Round Steal to MSG
description: Two nets cut down, a draft-night steal, a dad who ran the point, and a Garden captain—five steps into Brunson.
imageHint: The steady point guard in blue and orange, orchestrating plays with calm precision in pressure moments

questions.question: Before he was Madison Square Garden's clutch king, Brunson helped Villanova win how many national championships?
questions.explanation: Titles in 2016 and 2018. As a junior he was consensus National Player of the Year and Final Four all-tournament—then somehow slipped to the second round.

questions.question: After those two titles, Dallas took that Villanova star where in the 2018 NBA Draft—a pick that looks absurd in hindsight?
questions.explanation: Second-round pick 33. Four years later he walked into free agency as one of the league's most wanted guards—and New York pounced.

questions.question: That 33rd-overall steal left Dallas in 2022 and remade which Eastern Conference franchise overnight?
questions.explanation: A four-year deal that flipped the franchise. Villanova teammates Josh Hart and Donte DiVincenzo later joined him in orange and blue.

questions.question: The Knicks' new star grew up in gyms watching his dad run the point in the NBA—including a stop in New York. What is dad's name?
questions.explanation: Rick played nine seasons for eight teams and later coached. Jalen's game—pace, angles, no panic—is pure gym-rat inheritance from Cherry Hill to Lincolnshire.

questions.question: With Rick's old New York club now his team, Villanova retired what number for Jalen on Feb. 8, 2023—the day before the Knicks traded for Josh Hart?
questions.explanation: Retired in the Wells Fargo Center. Brunson was later named the 36th captain in Knicks history—the kid from the second round, running the Garden.

easterEgg.title: 56 in a state final
easterEgg.text: At Stevenson High in Illinois, Brunson dropped 56 points in an IHSA finals game—a state-final scoring record—against a team featuring future No. 1 pick Jahlil Okafor. The Garden saw that version coming; the draft board didn't.
